<description>
Found while auditing #36628

Already known upstream issue with C-tor: https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/core/tor/-/issues/32314

With `-proxy` pointed at Tor, outbound connections to IPv6 peers whose
 address contains an inner `::` always fail with "general failure".

 Core sends every SOCKS5 destination as a DOMAINNAME, with IPv6 in its
 compressed form. Tor copies the name into its relay BEGIN cell as
 `<name>:<port>`, and the exit's `tor_addr_port_split` first tries to parse
 the whole string as an IPv6 address. `2001:db8::1:8333` is a valid one,
 because the `::` absorbs the port as an eighth group. The exit then sees no
 port and closes the stream. Addresses written with all eight groups, or
 ending in `::`, are unaffected: appending `:port` to them does not give a
 valid address.

 About 20% of the IPv6 addresses in a gossip-filled addrman, and 29% of
 current IPv6 DNS seed answers, have an inner `::`. The failure is closed;
 there is no fallback to a direct connection.

 Note that this also effects private broadcast by default.

 This PR sends such addresses with all eight groups written out
 (`2001:db8:0:0:0:0:0:1`). `<name>:<port>` then has nine groups, so the exit
 splits at the last colon. Other forms:

 | Form                  | Tor         | Tor, SafeSocks 1 | getaddrinfo-based proxies |
 |-----------------------|-------------|------------------|---------------------------|
 | `2001:db8::1` (today) | fails       | fails            | works                     |
 | `[2001:db8::1]`       | works       | works            | fails                     |
 | ATYP IPv6             | works, logs a DNS-leak warning | refused | works         |
 | eight groups (this PR)| works       | works            | works                     |

 Tested against tor 0.4.9.13: on mainnet, master could not reach four
 seed-provided peers with inner-`::` addresses (30 "general failure"); with
 this change all four connected and completed the version handshake.
 `feature_proxy.py` and a new `netbase_tests` case check the bytes sent.
</description>

<commits>
721e2f5051 netbase: send shortened IPv6 addresses to SOCKS5 proxies in full

Tor copies a SOCKS5 DOMAINNAME into its relay BEGIN cell as
"<name>:<port>", and an exit parses "2001:db8::1:8333" as an IPv6
address with no port and closes the stream. Outbound connections
through a Tor -proxy to IPv6 addresses that contain "::" therefore fail
with "general failure". About a third of the IPv6 addresses the DNS
seeds return have this form.

Write such addresses with all eight groups. "<name>:<port>" is then not
an IPv6 address, so the exit splits it at the last colon, and the name
is still an address to proxies that resolve it with getaddrinfo, which
brackets would break.
</commits>
